issue.title: gateway: switching from Vertex Gemini to Antigravity sends a rejected thought signature
issue.body:
## What happens

In Magpie 0.1.1367, continuing a conversation after switching from the GCP AI plugin’s Vertex Gemini 4 Argon to the Antigravity `gemini-3.8-flash` provider returns:

```
400 Antigravity: Corrupted thought signature.
```

In the same conversation, switching from Vertex Gemini to GPT succeeds. The failure is reproducible on the Antigravity request path; no real Google model call is needed to understand the missing recovery branch.

## Why this appears to happen

Magpie preserves Gemini signatures in tool-call history and can put them back into Code Assist requests. In `internal/gateway/codeassist.go`, `buildCodeAssistSent` forwards `Part.Signature` as `thoughtSignature` (and does the same for signed text parts).

Magpie already has recovery for a Gemini signature rejected by Vertex AI: `internal/gateway/gateway.go` retries after `vertexSignatureRefused` and `withoutSignatures` in `internal/gateway/vertex.go`. But this retry is gated on `p.IsVertex()` and the matcher only recognizes `Invalid thought signature`. Antigravity is Code Assist, and reports `Corrupted thought signature`, so the existing recovery is skipped and the 400 is returned.

The local usage record for this report showed a successful Vertex Argon request, then Antigravity Flash 400, then a successful GPT request in the same session. The stored signature references for that session’s Argon tool calls were present and passed the sigstore hash check, so this does not look like a missing/corrupted local signature file. It is still possible the target rejects a complete signature because it came from a different backend/model; request-level comparison would establish that conclusively.

This is distinct from #1536: there a client truncates the tool-call ID/signature payload; here the signature references in the local store are intact and the target is Antigravity after a provider switch.

## Suggested fix

Extend the existing one-time signature-rejection recovery to Antigravity Gemini/Code Assist requests and recognize both `Invalid thought signature` and `Corrupted thought signature`. On that specific 400 only, retry a copied request with incompatible historical tool-call signatures removed, using the Code Assist path’s supported unsigned-history behavior. Keep the original request/history intact, retain signatures on normal same-provider continuation, and do not retry other 400s. Please account for signed text parts separately if they can also trigger this error.

## Regression tests

- Antigravity rejects a historical signature with `Corrupted thought signature`: retry once without the incompatible signature and succeed.
- Vertex’s existing `Invalid thought signature` retry remains unchanged.
- A successful same-provider tool-call continuation still carries its signature.
- Other 400 responses do not trigger a signature retry.
- Verify the behavior for tool-call signatures and, if applicable, text-part signatures.

Magpie 0.1.1367 source: `internal/gateway/codeassist.go`, `internal/gateway/gateway.go`, `internal/gateway/vertex.go`.

comments.body:
Root cause is exactly what you pointed at: the one-time recovery only existed for Vertex AI.

`internal/gateway/gateway.go` gated the retry on `p.IsVertex()`, and the matcher in `internal/gateway/vertex.go` only knew `Invalid thought signature`. Antigravity goes through `provider.CodeAssist` and says `Corrupted thought signature`, so the 400 went straight back to the client even though the Code Assist path can send that history unsigned (`skipSignature`).

Fixed on [fix/antigravity-signature](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/antigravity-signature) (`043636a3`, one commit on today's `main` `01468003`):

- the retry condition is now `p.IsVertex() || to == provider.CodeAssist`;
- the matcher accepts `(?i)(invalid|corrupted) thought signature`;
- `withoutSignatures` now clears signed text parts as well as tool-call signatures, on a copy, so the original request and the stored session history keep them. Signed text parts only reach the vendor from a Gemini/Responses client; the Code Assist envelope already drops thinking parts for an Anthropic client.
- boundaries unchanged: only that 400, only before anything was streamed to the client, one retry, and a request the target accepts keeps its signatures.

RED -> GREEN, re-run independently here:
- clean base `01468003` with only the new test file: `TestAntigravityRetriesCorruptedSignature` fails with your literal error, `400 Antigravity: Corrupted thought signature.`
- at the branch head: that test passes, along with `TestAntigravityDoesNotRetryOtherBadRequests` (another 400 on the same path is the client's - one request only) and the existing `TestVertexRetriesOnlyForVertex`, which checks a same-provider continuation still carries its signature.
- full `go test ./internal/gateway`, `go vet` and `go build` for linux, windows and `-tags nogui`: green. One pre-existing failure, `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged`, is red on the clean base too.

Honest limits: no real Google call. The Antigravity upstream in the test is a local server answering with the refusal in your report, so the retry being *accepted* by the real Code Assist service is not observed here. The text-part clearing is exercised by the same code path but only the tool-call case is asserted end to end.

Fixed on `fix/3572-antigravity-thought-signature` (ba8d930541fd0de69c46e6b87a0cf582085b8a0b):

When switching from Vertex Gemini to Antigravity, a "Corrupted
thought signature" 400 was not retried because the existing recovery
only matched Vertex's "Invalid thought signature" and was gated on
`p.IsVertex()`. Antigravity uses the same Code Assist API, so the same
signature retry logic applies.

Fix: extend the retry check to also match "Corrupted thought signature"
and apply for Antigravity (provider ID "antigravity"). Added
`corruptedThoughtSignature` regex in `internal/gateway/vertex.go`.

Test: existing Gemini signature tests pass (2 passed).

The fork commit ba8d930 only gates the retry on p.IsVertex() || p.ID == "antigravity", and it was never turned into a PR against this repo. main still has:

```
if p.IsVertex() && res.StatusCode == http.StatusBadRequest && vertexSignatureRefused.Match(b)
and vertex.go still only matches "(?i)invalid thought signature".
```

It also doesn't cover the google provider (Gemini Developer API), which reports the same 400. Reproduced on 0.1.2731:

1. google-vertex/gemini-4-argon tool call -> 200 (signature cached).
2. Same body to google/models/gemini-4-argon -> 400 Corrupted thought signature.
3. Delete that one cache file -> the same body returns 200.

Direct API check: Vertex returns the raw signature (116 chars, 85 bytes, prefix 018f3d6b...). The Developer API expects the protobuf envelope (120 chars, 12 57 0a 55 + raw). Sending the raw Vertex signature -> 400; wrapping the same bytes -> 200.

Minimal fix: include p.ID == "google" (or any non-Vertex Gemini endpoint) in the retry condition. withoutSignatures already yields a request that succeeds there (skip_thought_signature_validator is accepted). Longer term, the sigstore should store or normalize the envelope for the target endpoint instead of replaying it verbatim.

issue.title: gateway: foreign non-base64 thoughtSignature (anthropic-thinking-v1:…) reaches Gemini clients verbatim; strict clients (Antigravity CLI) reject the whole turn

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**TL;DR (EN):** When an upstream (a relay bridging an Anthropic-protocol model) puts the common `anthropic-thinking-v1:<base64(JSON)>` thinking envelope into a tool call's signature slot, magpie forwards that string **verbatim** as `parts[].thoughtSignature` to Gemini-protocol clients. `thoughtSignature` is a proto `bytes` field and must be base64 on the wire, so strict Go clients (Antigravity CLI / agy) fail to unmarshal the whole `GenerateContentResponse` and the turn dies: `illegal base64 data at input byte 9`. Suggestion below: base64-wrap foreign signatures on the way out to Gemini clients and unwrap on the way back (the mirror of the `__tsr` idea that already exists for ids), or drop invalid values instead of forwarding them.

## 环境

- magpie 桌面版 **0.1.3078**,Windows(10.0.26300)
- 客户端:Antigravity CLI(agy,Go 实现),走 magpie 的 Gemini `streamGenerateContent` 端点
- 上游 provider:某第三方中转(已脱敏,下文记作 `<relay>`),模型 `gemini-4-carbon`;该中转的上游实际是 Anthropic Messages 协议(响应 id 形如 `msg_…`)

## 现象

**间歇性**出现(有几率):某一回合的「思考 + 工具调用」响应被客户端整体拒绝,agy 报:

```text
⚠ agent executor error: generating and executing: mapToStruct: error unmarshalling input
map[string]interface {}{"candidates":[]map[string]interface {}{map[string]interface {}
{"content":map[string]interface {}{"parts":[]interface {}{map[string]interface {}
{"functionCall":map[string]interface {}{"args":map[string]interface {}
{"Path":"<workspace>\\tools\\test-biomes.mjs","StartLine":1},
"id":"call_6069…","name":"read_file"},
"thoughtSignature":"anthropic-thinking-v1:eyJ0aGlua2luZyI6…"}}, "role":"model"}, "index":0}},
"modelVersion":"<relay>/gemini-4-carbon", "responseId":"msg_e3e7…"}
: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field
.candidates.0.content.parts.0.thoughtSignature of type []uint8:
illegal base64 data at input byte 9
```

## 出错的响应长什么样

`thoughtSignature` 的值形如 `anthropic-thinking-v1:<base64>`,base64 解开是:

```json
{"thinking":"…(思考文本,已隐去)","signature":"","type":"thinking"}
```

即:中转把 **Anthropic thinking block** 用 `anthropic-thinking-v1:` 信封 + base64 打包,塞进了 signature 槽位 —— 这是不少 Anthropic 桥接实现里通用的「无损搬运 thinking」做法。它**不是合法 base64**:`anthropic-thinking-v1` 的第 9 个字节是 `-`,不在 base64 字母表里,所以 Go 端 `encoding/json` 把 string 解进 `[]byte` 时正好在 byte 9 报错。

## 为什么是间歇性的

只有当这一步模型**先思考、再发起工具调用**(signature 槽位非空)时才触发:

- 纯文本回复、或不带思考块的工具调用 → 没有这个字段 → 正常
- 一旦带上了 → 严格客户端把整个响应拒掉,回合中断

## 链路分析(对着 main @ 52c9880)

进站有两条可能路径(取决于该 provider 在 magpie 里配置的协议),出站汇合在同一处:

1. **Chat 兼容上游**:中转在 `tool_calls[].extra_content.google.thought_signature` 给出该信封;`(*chatDecoder).toolCall`(internal/gateway/chat.go:1554)→ `signedID(id, googleSignature(...))`,非 canonical base64 按设计记作 `__tsr<n>__<base64url(原文)>` 骑在 id 上(internal/gateway/gemini_signature.go:60)。
2. **Gemini 原生上游**:`sigTidy{native: true}`(internal/gateway/gateway.go:7325-7327)对上游字节做透传(仅 note signer),`thoughtSignature` 原样流过 —— `sigTidy.lines` 目前只 tidy 蛇形的 `"thought_signature"`(Chat 的 extra_content),camelCase 的 `"thoughtSignature"` 不在检查范围。

出站点(两条路径都会经过):

- `geminiParts` 的 ToolCall 分支(internal/gateway/gemini.go:653-663):`unsignedID` 取回签名**原文**,原样写进 `part["thoughtSignature"]`;Text part(gemini.go:641)与 `KTextSig`(gemini.go:745)同理。
- 本次报错 JSON 的形状(`candidates[0] = {content:{parts, role:"model"}, index:0}` + `modelVersion` + `responseId`,无 finishReason/usage)与 `geminiEncoder.chunk`(gemini.go:691)的输出完全一致。

而 Gemini API 的 `thoughtSignature` 是 proto `bytes`,JSON 线上必须是 base64;agy 用 `encoding/json` 解进 `[]byte` 时(Std + padding 的严格解码),在 `-`(byte 9)上解码失败,整包被拒。任何按 protojson/bytes 语义解析的严格 Gemini 客户端都会一样挂。

## 建议

出站到 Gemini 协议客户端时,保证 `thoughtSignature` 恒为合法 base64:

- **首选**:对非 canonical base64 的外来签名,出站时 base64 包一层(magpie 可识别的标记,用 `StdEncoding`,因为 `encoding/json` 解 `[]byte` 只认 std + padding);客户端下一轮把 `thoughtSignature` 原样带回来时(internal/gateway/gemini.go:356 已在读回)解包还原成逐字节一致的原文 —— 正好是 id 里 `__tsr` 思路的镜像。解包需要发生在 `noteSigner` / `foreignSignature` 的 provider 归属匹配之前,签名归属才不受影响。
- **保底**:写不合法值时宁可不写(丢掉这个 signature),也不要原样透传让严格客户端拒整包。
- 两个写入点(gemini.go:641 / gemini.go:745)与 Gemini 原生透传路径(gateway.go:7325-7327)需要同样的出站校验。

## 相关

- #1445(lossless reasoning state transport across Chat / Responses / Anthropic / Gemini)
- #3572(switching from Vertex Gemini to Antigravity sends a rejected thought signature)
